utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed that the witness was not yet available near to the courtroom. I take it that he will arrive soon. Meanwhile, I did understand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you wanted to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. With your permission, of course. Thank you very much. It will take me only a few minutes. I wish to indicate more or less the same thing as I brought up last time but concerning a different matter. We have received your written decision concerning the admissibility of the depositions of what we should call expert witnesses, Madam Tabeau and Mr. Philips. We wish to indicate that we intend to write very soon a document pursuant to 73(B), that is, lodge leave to appeal your decision. However, there is the time consideration. I don't know whether that will be taken care of before the depositions -- before the testimony of Madam Tabeau and Mr. Philips. If we have to examine these two witnesses before a decision -- final decision is reached, we will have to do that only under certain reservations. So we will have to leave -- to wait for the leave to lodge an appeal pursuant to Rule 73(B). That was the only thing that I wanted to indicate. And one more thing, I will be obliged to leave the session tomorrow somewhat earlier for reasons of my travel arrangements. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the Chamber will give due consideration to the fact that if there is still an opportunity to ask for certificate for appeal, whether examining the witness would interfere with this right, we will consider that and I will discuss the matter within the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If there is still a few minutes, perhaps I could use the time by raising two matters, if that is convenient to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, it depends on how much -- I mean, if these are matters that will take more time, then we should do it later, but if these are just small matters, then we could do it now. Because I know that the witness is in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I will stop as soon as he is available, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And how do we know that he is available? Will the usher -- ? Yes, the usher will tell us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the first matter is simply to note that it seems at this stage we are unlikely to finish the proposed timetable for the week. We still have Messrs. Fraser, Bergeron, and one day of Richard Philips' testimony to go. Perhaps the witness is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel be asked to speak into the microphone or come closer to the microphone. We had problems hearing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, good morning. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. And the cross-examination will be resumed now. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I was informed that there was some difficulties in hearing you, so if you would please speak into the microphone as good as you can. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that my microphone was not on. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you aware of two incidents which took place on the 7th of November, 1992, and the 13th of December, 1992, respectively? I am referring to the incidents of sniping. Witness?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall specifically incidents of sniping on that occasion that separate those incidents from any other activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, yesterday you spoke about a distance of 500 to 600 yards when you talked about the depth of the front. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that behind this first, so to speak, technical zone, there was a logistical zone and then a command zone after that one. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the depth was of these two rear zones, that is, the logistical one and the command zone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is applying an exact science to something that isn't that exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I fully agree with you. But can you just give us an idea?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The resupply of the front line within the city would, of course, use many routes to fulfill their task. You would be unable to be specific in terms of a zone or an area for resupply.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you the following question: To the extent that these rear zones were used for logistical or command purposes, was it -- could these zones be identified as zones of a military character? Could that constitute a military target?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would not be zones of a military character. They would be supplies, items required on the front line, passing through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I should now like to go back to your statement, the one you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. Is it true that you stated that the mobile mortars which you were aware of enabled the Sarajevo army to find inside the town sheltered places, sheltered points, from which they could open fire and that the idea was to let the Serbs believe that they actually had more mortars, more pieces of mortar than they did?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a fair assessment, plus the tactical advantage of moving around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me now quote from your statement to the OTP, and I should like to have your confirmation of what you said. [In English] From the Bosnian Serbs in regard to the use of precision weapons against civilians." [Interpretation] Do you remember that portion of your statement, page 00520509?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, when that was read out, I had rather significant interference, so I was unable to understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am very sorry. Let me repeat. [In English] Receive protests from the Bosnian Serbs in regards to the use of Presidency weapons against civilians."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I missed --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In other words --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The problem is that there needs to be a pause when my learned colleague switches from French to English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I'm truly sorry. Let me try once again. [In English] "I did, however, receive protests from the Bosnian Serbs in regards to the use of Presidency weapons against civilians." [Interpretation] The word that does not appear, and I don't know why, is "Bosnian."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and apart from that, I take it that you were talking about Presidency weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Presidency, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it was about protests from the Bosnian Serbs about the use of Presidency weapons. And the rest you heard, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Yes, I recall that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me continue quoting from your statement. My next quotation concerns the weapons that the Presidency had at -- on Mount Igman, if you remember. I am indicating these weapons to you in order to save time. [In English] "One 130 millimetres, one Howitzer, four 105-millimetre field guns, two 122-millimetre field guns, and six 120-millimetre mortars." [Interpretation] Do you remember these figures? Are they correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall those figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me now move to another issue. In your statement, did you not state that the Presidency intended to use, in political terms, its status of a victim, allegedly?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also state that, in your mind, the Bosnian forces were responsible for bringing fire by their conduct, for bringing fire down on to themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think it appropriate that my friend read the words to the witness, since the witness does not have a copy of his statement in front of him and it is many years since he wrote it. I don't require, in the interest of saving time, that the witness be given a copy of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness -- well, first of all, first question is: If there is -- I do understand that there is no objection against the way the statement is summarised.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I also need to check the statement, preferably before the witness responds, and when my friend is simply summarising what is in the statement, I would be grateful for not only a page reference but also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are still uncertain about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be happy to do so, Mr. President, however, I am afraid that it will take a bit more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will quote in English your statement, witness. "In my mind, the Bosnians --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps my friend could indicate the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already indicated the page: 510. I repeat, 510, the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I quote, in English, with a pause: [In English] "In my mind, the Bosnians were in such occasions responsible for bringing fire down upon the hospital. I also know that the Presidency forces would sometimes drive one of their tanks around in the same vicinity. This, I felt, was a direct provocation to the Serbs to shoot at it." [Interpretation] Did you state this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, now I have a few very specific questions concerning other facts during your tenure in Sarajevo. Were you aware of an attack which took place against Serb civilians? Were you aware of the attacks which took place against Serb civilians on the 27th and the 28th of November, 1992, which resulted in the death of seven civilians?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you indicate where that attack took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This attack took place in the area of Jahorina. Also, an attack on a bus carrying a number of civilians, which resulted in the death of three of those civilians, in the area of Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, did you lodge a protest with the Sarajevo forces?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't, but I believe that is the reason I heard of the incident, because it was reported in UNPROFOR headquarters Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of an attack which took place -- are you aware of the attacks coming from Mount Igman on the 4th and 8th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be specific about the 4th and 8th of December, 1992, because it was a frequent occurrence that the weapons on Mount Igman were used in the conflict, and I recall specifically that they were used and fired upon the area of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. When you say, "Ilidza," are you referring to a civilian area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The whole battle area was occupied by civilians, hence, it is a city called Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So are you telling us that Muslim forces had opened fire on an area in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Ilidza, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That is a part of Sarajevo, on an area in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a suburb of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Speaking of the 24th of October, 1992, could you perhaps be more specific, do you know that an attack on civilians on that date resulted in the death of eight small children? The area in question was Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't specifically recall that incident, but if it has been reported to UNPROFOR and UN military observers, it will be included in the records.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, did you personally see in Sarajevo, in the town of Sarajevo, columns of men who -- going to the front line for the purposes of rotation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That would be oversimplistic. Resupply in columns would be a very natural military target and so, clearly, resupply occurred at night-time, undercover, and not in large parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the rotation was done in night-time, in small groups?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that the Bosnian forces would have used concealment to protect their soldiers and their supplies and would, therefore, not have been obvious about their procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. May I conclude on the basis of your answer that this could take place at night-time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five more minutes, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am strictly keeping you to five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can I therefore conclude, Witness, yes or no, that this also took place at night-time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can I also conclude, Witness, that if this was concealed -- if this has been concealed, the UN forces would have also been able to observe this? I am sorry, the opposite, that the UN forces would not have been able to observe this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew it was happening. It is a natural and normal military procedure, and individual observers had seen these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I quote what you stated in -- from your statement, page 110112, page 12. You declared the following concerning the shelling. I will quote in English: [In English] "All fire that was incoming to the city of Sarajevo was analysed along what the objectives of that fire would be. If it wasn't seen to be in response to any military events, one can only assume that the indiscriminate fire was being used to fashion terror because there was no military objective." Can you recall this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if you declared this, if this is what you stated indeed, how, since you didn't know where all of the fixed military -- fixed or mobile military objectives were in Sarajevo, how was it possible for you to declare that the shelling in question was indiscriminate, that is -- I rephrase the question. I will ask it in different terms, in order to save time. Can you categorically exclude before this Chamber the possibility that there was a military or mobile -- there was a fixed or mobile military target in one of these shellings inside the town, in allegedly civilian areas?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I personally moved around the city, I met many individuals who lived in Sarajevo in blocks of flats and other buildings. I was clearly capable from my own observations of estimating whether these buildings were being used for military purpose. Because I didn't and had no requirement to understand where all the military buildings were, I had the ability to determine where they were not. These buildings which were not used were also extensively damaged by this fire which I have described in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, but you did not answer my question. I was speaking about -- also about mobile targets. Could you absolutely exclude speaking before this Chamber that regardless of which target that you are talking about, that there were not some mobile targets such as mortars as you have described, or unit taking on shift or leaving shift, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now your question is slightly different. You are talking about mobile targets, i.e. weapons. I was talking of headquarters and other command and control buildings. The mobile targets were not that numerous and we were able to observe them and, yes, they would be fair targets for the Serb side to try to counter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this was your last question. It is now six minutes instead of five.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It hasn't been answered. The question was: "Could you definitely exclude that?" And it was not answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you definitely exclude it, Mr. Mole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exclude what, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exclude that firing which you would consider indiscriminate would target any of such mobile or, for you, hidden military objects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I answer your question quite specifically then relating to an incident which we did investigate. And that was that the hospital at Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would ask you whether you could categorically exclude that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were incidents where it was possible it could occur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say sometimes it could, but perhaps not always.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in relation to the last quote that Mr. Piletta-Zanin gave, he said it was on page 12. I can't find that quote on page 12. Perhaps he could check the reference and tell me what page it was on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is on page 11012, line 21. But these are old markings, Mr. Ierace. One has to go back to the original text. But I believe that -- but I believe that the quote was correct. It was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, does that mean that the quote was from the transcript of the witness's earlier evidence and not the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is exactly what I said, Mr. Ierace. Exactly what I said. Any problems with this quote?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The English transcript indicates the word "statement," Mr. President, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's not discuss it. When the word "statement" is used, we usually refer to the statement. When we use the word "testimony," we usually refer to what was earlier --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't following the transcript, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, you were asked questions yesterday and today about fire being directed from Kosevo, the vicinity of Kosevo hospital, by mobile mortars. Is it your understanding from what you were told that it was a case of, to use the vernacular, "shoot and scoot," in other words, a round or two would be fired from the back of a mobile mortar and, within seconds, it would depart?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that there would be at some point thereafter return fire from Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that the return fire would target the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would attempt to target the mobile unit that it was aiming to destroy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If that was the case, would it not follow that the return fire, firstly, would have to be within seconds; and secondly, would not impact on the buildings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: One would hope that the return fire was quick in response to the outgoing fire. Of course, it often wasn't, and we well know the accuracy of artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there involved in the retaliatory fire, from your perception, any element of punishment, in other words, sending a message that if fire was permitted from the hospital grounds, then the hospital would be deliberately hit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was always a degree of overkill in response --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must object to this question because this idea of "punishment" implies subjective will, and the witness cannot know anything about that. It is not a fact. It is the intent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. If you would ask, please do it in a more factual way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to the lapse of time between the outgoing and incoming fire and having regard also to the site at which the incoming fire would land, did you form any opinion as to whether there was an element of retribution behind the return fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, but this is one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not the same thing, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, and as you may have noticed, sometimes the forming of an opinion on what might have moved someone else has been the subject of questioning by both parties. So, therefore, it is not the same and, of course, the Chamber will assess and will have to be very careful in evaluating answers to questions like this one. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Perhaps you better repeat the question or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please answer it then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The imbalance between the number of rounds which were outgoing from the Presidency side and the number that were returned in apparent response was such that it was heavily in favour of the Serb side. One can draw what conclusions one wishes from that. Those were the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it the case that the hospital itself was frequently hit in the context of the return fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday, you were asked questions about whether in the basement of the building occupied by United Nations forces there was in fact an arms factory operated by, presumably, forces of the Bosnian government. And you said this: "It was unfounded information in that being the senior military officer, I had to be sure in my mind that the PTT building was not being used for such inappropriate activity. I confirmed that that had not been the case. There was an engineering workshop but it was not producing any munitions, not during my tour." First of all, the building being used --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President,

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply wish to say the same as before. The Defence spoke about basements or about cellars, because we want to say that this shop is right next to the PTT building and we wish to check this merely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right that you were literally quoting the witness's testimony of yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am quoting a note I made of that. I handwrote it yesterday during the cross-examination. I am happy to find the passage on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then for the transcript, it should be -- it is stated as a quote in the transcript. We should be careful with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is on page 44 -- 44, line 13, 11044, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it on 17 but that might be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question, in English, quite clearly put the proposition, and I now quote: "That there was an ammunition factory in the basement of the PTT building."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, was the UN headquarters in the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the PTT building, at least before the war, if not during it? Did it have some relationship to communications?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the headquarters of the telephone service in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did it, or at least part of the building, function as such during your time there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Communications were maintained throughout that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The engineering workshop that you said was in the basement, I take it, given your previous answers, that its apparent purpose was to provide engineering services for telephone services. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did UN staff ever take refuge in that basement from time to time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Often.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that in circumstances where shells were exploding nearby or on the building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, from time to time, unexpectedly, were UN staff required to, without any warning, invade the basement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that it was unfounded information. Where did it come from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a rumour that we heard persistently from a number of sources from the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear the claim being made by anyone in the United Nations staff, in the building itself?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the suggestion that the basement was being used? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said also in that answer that you confirmed that the allegation was unfounded. How did you do that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I physically checked the building. I was overly familiar with that building, having spent so much of my time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you said yesterday that in relation to Nedzarici that General Galic raised it with you; I think you implied more than once. What were his concerns about Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that it was an enclave in the city and an extremely tenuous hold within it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was he seeking any specific measures from the UN in relation to it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the rationale for the request to have a UN OP in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given its position in relation to the front line, that is, from a Serb army perspective, it is a forward position, was it both vulnerable, since it was surrounded on three sides by Bosnian government forces, but at the same time, did it afford a position of greater access to Bosnian Serb territory for the same reason?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in that it's an enclave into the city, it would be exactly that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that it was very difficult to confirm that a shooting incident was, in fact, a matter of a civilian having been deliberately or indiscriminately shot. You didn't use those words but I think that fairly puts what you were driving at. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The definition between sniping, if I recall correctly, and general fire, was the point I was making.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given that observation by you, does that apply throughout the city and in particular to intersections where containers had been set up Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. or other anti-sniping barriers? In other words, does it have uniform application or were there some areas where you would take a different view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The context was the front line in answer to my question yesterday, which related to that confusion. Elsewhere in the city, that confusion was less confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you also were asked questions about the desire by the Serb forces for Sarajevo to be demilitarised. What was the proposal, as you understood it, that the Serb forces were putting in terms of a demilitarisation of the war?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of these discussions were perpetrated through the mixed military working group and the proposals which were presented to all sides were often UN driven, as opposed to driven by one side or the other. So in answer to your question, I don't recall anything but Serb response and Presidency response to the UN proposals.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it in the context of those UN-driven discussions that the ceasefire came into being, that is, that a ceasefire was negotiated to take effect on around the 11th of November?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Exhibit 358.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asked to -- I was asked to finish quickly and Mr. Ierace was to have ten minutes, and these ten minutes have been long past. So I would like to hear your reaction

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will tell you my reaction. I am telling you my reaction. Yesterday, I said you had a quarter of an hour left. You used today more than 25 minutes. And I did write down from the last five minutes - and let me just check - from the first four of the five minutes, the witness spoke for a bit over one minute. All the rest of the time was used by putting questions to the witness. So, therefore, having warned you in advance, given that you knew since yesterday that you had not more than a quarter of an hour, if you then use most of the time for putting questions and repeating questions, then I said after six minutes that it was finished. I will keep a close eye, and the Chamber keeps a close eye not only on how much time the parties use but also on how they use it. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In a general sense, in the early entries for that month, do you occasionally refer to UN meetings, in particular, the military mixed working group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please go to the entry for the 7th of November, 1992, in particular, the last six or seven lines of the first paragraph. If you count up eight lines, halfway through that line, do these words appear: "Again, it must be concluded that although the Serb delegation are willing to go through the motions of attendance at the MMWG and its subcommittees, they appear to have little attention of abandoning their previously stated positions. In particular, there seems little reason to believe that the Serbs have any -- "

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry I was listening to the French interpretation and the French booth wasn't listening. I am taking 30 seconds. I have to listen to what the French booth is saying. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "In particular, there seems little reason to believe that the Serb -- "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not understand exactly. The translation was that you were listening to the French interpretation and the French booth wasn't listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We have major problems with interpretation and just a moment ago I was misinterpreted with what I just said. What the French booth said is that they could not hear certain things, so could Mr. Ierace start his question once again so that the transcript could be -- could catch up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might also be a matter of speed, Mr. Ierace. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Repeat the quote, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The entire quote, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "Again it must be concluded that although the Serb delegation are willing to go through the motions of attendance at the MMWG and its subcommittees, they appear to have little intention of abandoning their previously stated positions. In particular, there seems little reason to believe that the Serbs have any intention of abandoning their off-stated principle that they are in favour of either complete ceasefire and demilitarisation simultaneously across BH or none at all."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that -- were those words written by you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry. But one should quote it to the end because the end is just as important, and I believe that Mr. Ierace could also make this effort and read to the end of the passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am happy to do that, Mr. President. I accept that principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "As piecemeal demilitarisation would allow the Presidency to concentrate their forces in other areas, the viewpoint of the Serbs is understandable." Those words were also written by you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do the words reflect your view both now and at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do exactly. The solution for Sarajevo was integral to the solution for BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And as part of that, when you agree that the Serb forces wanted peace in Sarajevo, was that a non-negotiable and integral part of a proposal that there be a ceasefire across Bosnia-Herzegovina and all the territory which they held, they kept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was their preference, so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I ask you, you indicated ten minutes yesterday. How much time would you still think you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just a few minutes, Mr. President, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I will keep you to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, this morning, the passage was quoted to you from your statement. This line was quoted to you: "I did, however, receive protests from the Bosnian Serbs in regard to the use of Presidency weapons against civilians." I read on for the principle: "These mainly related to the shelling of Ilidza by Presidency forces on Igman to which the Bosnian Serb forces under Galic would threaten to shell Sarajevo." Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When General Galic threatened to retaliate by shelling Sarajevo, did you have any understanding as to whether that threat was to use indiscriminate fire or to fire against legitimate military targets?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that the number of incoming rounds on the city would increase, but you will appreciate the difficulty of tracking the specific intention of every round.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any particular -- I withdraw that. Did you have any particular view as to whether the threat by him in those circumstances, that is, the fire against civilians on the Serb side did not stop, whether he was sending a message that the same sort of fire would be given in return, that is, against civilians?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My experience in the military indicates that the incoming fire was of too general a nature to be specifically targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, finally, you were asked about some incidents involving casualties of Serbian civilians and you were also asked about some fire from Igman on the 4th and 8th of December, 1992. And you said essentially that you recollected that there was fire into the Ilidza area from Mount Igman at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is Ilidza immediately adjacent to Otes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And on those -- were those two dates within the Otes operation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether the fire from Mount Igman on those dates from Bosnian government positions was targeted towards legitimate military targets or civilian targets?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were legitimate military targets within Ilidza, for I visited them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you, Mr. Mole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The first question is related to your -- the previous question by Mr. Ierace. How far is Ilidza from Otes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3, 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 7th of June, you mentioned an incident in which some UNMOs were held illegally on the Serb side and they were released after the intervention or the embodiment of the military police, and that was at the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions on that. The first one is: Who held those UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building they were resident within was occupied by the owners, and the owners had lost a son in the conflict and were unable to retrieve the body. And, obviously, a combination of distress caused them to take the action they did, to hold the UNMOs, to use them as a hostage to achieve their objective of the return of the body of their relative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: And the military police was the Serb Military Police?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, I should like to ask you a question as follows: How did you become aware of the shelling around the hospital -- the Kosevo hospital? Did you personally see the incident or was the incident reported to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My subsector commander, Flight Lieutenant Carl Harding, commanded his UNMOs in the city. He did a series of investigations on both hospitals, to clarify the degree of likelihood that the hospitals were being targeted deliberately as opposed to in response to these mobile units. It was as a result of his investigation, plus the observation of his UNMOs, that we were able to give you the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand your testimony correctly, the rounds originated from the mortars located around a hospital, that is, the Kosevo hospital. You spoke about two hospitals, however, that were targeted, if I understand you correctly. The other hospital was not a place where a military target such as a mobile mortar was located. It was only from the Kosevo hospital that the mortars opened fire. Is that correct? Do I interpret correctly your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You understand it as relates to that single incident, but there were incidents where the same tactic was used, not only in that one hospital but others and the PTT building and other buildings occupied by the UN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one last question to you directly related to the question of Judge El Mahdi. When you say, "the same tactic was used at other occasions, other buildings," would that include the other hospital? Because the question was about two hospitals, and the answer was about Kosevo hospital and other buildings. Would that include, well, let's say the State or French hospital, or were you talking about other buildings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would include the other hospitals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would include the other hospitals?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then ask you: Was there enough space to station a mobile mortar around or on the premises of the French or State Hospital?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anywhere one could drive a vehicle, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did that happen at many occasions at the other hospital?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Numerically, it's very difficult to answer that question, but I would put it down as frequent occurrence, but there wasn't a rash of that activity. It would be inclusive within the tactics that were employed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see both parties are on their feet. May I take it they both want to ask additional questions in relation to what the Judges asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should add that I would seek to say something in the absence of the witness before I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Mole, I have to ask you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to avoid bringing back the witness, who has spent a lot of time waiting, would you please allow me to ask one question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what the Prosecution would like to submit to the Court. I mean, if that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not even a question. It is just a statement which is very clear on the part of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know what Mr. Ierace wants to submit to the Court. Would an additional question or what is not actually a question, as I do understand Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would that interfere with what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is just a very simple matter, Mr. President. Following the questions that were -- that have just been asked and also following what the Prosecution has declared, it is clear that General Galic disputes ever saying, and consequently to this witness as well, that he would shell the city in response to any action or in form of retaliation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what has the Prosecution declared --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It was following a quotation given by the Prosecution involving witness's words. And since the quotation, literally speaking, I am trying to quote now, [In English] "forces under Galic" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that what the text says?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Exactly sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it was quoting a text.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In due course, of course, you can make whatever observations you like, but this is not the time for argument at this moment. So, therefore, I will not allow you to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will try to avoid the submission in the absence of the witness. If I can be allowed to ask one or two questions, that might render it unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Questions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, in relation to what you have just said about the State Hospital - not Kosevo, but the State Hospital - you referred to an investigation carried out by Carl Harding. Was that your only source of information about what happened at the State Hospital, as you understood it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Plus other information that we received from other UNPROFOR units deployed within Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I do need to make a submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do need or you do not need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mole, I will ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, in the course of responding to questions asked from the Bench, this witness has said, in effect, that mortars were fired from the State Hospital. That is contrary to all of the evidence on that topic in the Prosecution case so far. And that evidence includes the evidence of Carl Harding, the administrator, the surgeon, the journalist who lived in the hospital, and so on. It has never before been said or suggested. The fact that it is now said requires me to ask further questions of the witness which may go beyond one or two questions, which is what I now seek the opportunity to do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. The Defence opposes this request. This situation can be perfectly compared to a number of other situations, a number of other cases, when your Chamber told us, in particular the Defence, that we had -- we would have enough opportunity to ask these questions during the cross-examination that is, that we had had enough opportunity to do that during the cross-examination and that we could no longer do it. So I don't see any reason why the Prosecution should now be allowed to proceed with these additional questions. They had ample opportunity to bring it up during their examination. The fact that the witness has said something which might be contrary to other testimonies has nothing to do with the issue. It will be up to you as professional judges to compare these testimonies and place them in a context. The Prosecution had a team of three expert lawyers who had ample opportunity to ask these questions during their time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... clarify an answer the witness gave in response to questions of the Judges. As you may have noticed, we always allowed the parties to put additional questions if the issue was raised specifically during the questioning by the Judges. So that is the difference. So it could not have been dealt with at an earlier stage. Apart from that, I think -- the Chamber thinks it is an important issue. It does not mean that the Prosecution could just continue to ask questions, but a few questions we will allow, and the Defence will have an opportunity to ask additional questions in that respect as well. I think, Mr. Ierace, you said two would not be enough? The Chamber has in mind that would listen to your first five questions and then see how far we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I should add, of course, that there was no mention of this in either of the two statements of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We do not know that, but please proceed, after the witness has been brought in again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mole, there will be another few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned a few minutes ago that -- I withdraw that. You have given evidence that your statement, that is, your first statement, was made in September of 1997. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And in that statement you mentioned, I think, Kosevo hospital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, I did, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Specifically, the firing of mortars from Kosevo hospital. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you make any mention of the State Hospital in the same context in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't recall, but the reason for my mentioning the State Hospital was because of the question posed to me about other buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And in relation to other buildings, you mentioned as well the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you used the phrase "other hospitals," plural.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other buildings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recollect at this stage what the other sources of information were in respect of the State Hospital, that is, other than the investigation of Carl Harding?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if I can recall that mention was made during the morning meetings in the UNPROFOR headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you have any actual recollection of what was said at those meetings in respect of the State Hospital or are you saying that that is the only other possible source?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the only other source that I can recall, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, just so I can understand what you are telling us, are you saying that you distinctly recollect something was said at those meetings on the State Hospital?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recollect on how many occasions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than once or twice that I can recall, sir. That is not very exact, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recollect who it was that said something about the State Hospital at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have come from the operations room briefing as part of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did Carl Harding attend those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who else attended those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Representatives of all departments of UNPROFOR, plus the -- myself as the Senior Military Observer, UNHCR, Red Cross, if they were represented, and other agencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If there had been mortars fired from the vicinity of the State Hospital, who would you expect amongst those participants, if any, to have observed that or received that information?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the question is not relevant. Its purpose is to complete the submission of the Prosecution and not to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I strongly disagree with that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please respond to that, why --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would expect the source of that information to come from the UNPROFOR Battalions within Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I invited Mr. Ierace to respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, the complaint by my friend is that it is not relevant. So let me explain briefly the relevance. It is simply to establish, firstly, the sources of information; and secondly, the degree of recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the question has been answered now so it is of no use any more to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is my last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is your last question. When I said "five questions," I had in mind approximately five minutes, taking that a question and an answer usually take approximately one minute. So, therefore, there were more questions but it was put in approximately this time frame. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But before, we should like to have a moment to confer. The moment to take the break is coming near, so we will take the opportunity to confer with General Galic in order to clarify certain questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... now, we might conclude before having the break. So I give you one or two minutes to confer with General Galic and then we will see whether we can conclude at the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will try to restrict myself in view of the 14 questions that have been asked by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you stated it was possible to open fire from mortars from all of the locations that were accessible by a vehicle. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as long as it is relevant for where the weapon is firing to and it is within range.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Which means, finally, that every building normally accessible by road could be used as a shelter -- as a cover for the fire from a mortar, technically speaking?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Consequently, other buildings such as schools or places of worship would also be used for this purpose?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, whether that was the case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have indicated it was most probable and the frequency, however, was not great.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, technically speaking --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President -- just a moment, Witness. Mr. President, the interpreters are asking me to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, consequently, and again technically speaking, one can imagine that the famous library which burnt down in Sarajevo could also be used for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Not one of these questions arises from questions answered in response to -- I am sorry. Not one of these questions relates to topics raised by Your Honours' questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was about buildings as well, buildings, the hospital being one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the last question was about a building which was burnt down before General Galic took over the command of the SRK. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is a different issue. And you say we are out of the time frame. Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you refer to your sources in terms of operation rooms briefings. Did they include specialists, that is, the individuals who were knowledgeable when it comes to their mission?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You, personally, do you know -- are you aware of an incident which would have involved places of worship in this period -- in the relevant period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, your objection is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The same reason. This goes well beyond what questions were asked by Your Honours and this is indeed an issue -- it certainly was not a fresh issue, and that is the important point, not just that it is a matter raised by Your Honours, but that it is a matter which had not risen previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we are not talking about incidents Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in general, even not in places of worship or hospitals. What we are talking about was firing of mortars nearby buildings such as the State Hospital. So we will allow you to ask questions about that. But before doing so, may I ask you one clarification. You responded to one of the questions -- I will ask for two clarifications. You said that whatever buildings were accessible by a vehicle that could be used as shelter to technically, you said, "yes." And the next question was: "Consequently, other buildings such as schools or places of worship would also be used for this purpose?" You said, "Yes." And the next question was: "Do you know, Witness, whether that was the case?" And then you said: "I have indicated it was most probable and the frequency, however, was not great." I have some difficulties in combining the probability and a frequency. If I say it is possible that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because answering questions "yes or no," when they are complex, leads one to confusion. One has to relate my "yes" or "no" to the military capability of the BH side. They didn't have that many mortars of the sufficient range to permit more than one or two units that we are talking about to perform these tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But now my first question is: You answered in the affirmative that schools and places of worship were not only places where you could do such a thing like firing mobile mortars, but that they were used to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that it was technically possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we have the confusion. That is why I asked for the clarification. If you are talking about a probability, what you say is after you first answered the question is that was the case. I mean, what was the case? Was the case that it was possible or was the case that it was done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the case that it was possible. Because one responds again with the resources that we have, which wasn't sufficient to cover all the city all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge or were there any reports to you that mortars were fired from places of worship or schools?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. But, of course, we are five minutes over the -- I don't know whether you have many more questions. I tried to conclude before the break. How many questions would you still have?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have only two more questions, but three minutes were taken by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of course, if the interpreters - we will have then a break until 10 minutes past 11.00 - would be capable of helping us out for another three minutes. I see some nodding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said that the fact that Bosniak forces opened fire from all the hospitals made part of a certain tactic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. That was not the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you quote the witness, would you please be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Page 28 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The technique was used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Ierace, would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will read it out, 28.25. Page 28, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you use these words, "the tactic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that makes no sense, whether the word "tactic" was used if there is no context, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. So if you would please read that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am looking it up. But I am afraid my numbering is not identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I rose to my feet to help. Page 28, line 12, is the question. The answer follows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question was: "When you say the same tactic was used at other occasions, other buildings," reference was made to, I think, the answer you gave to a question of Judge El Mahdi. Yes. Your answer was -- it is page 28, line 4: "You understand it as relates to that single incident, but there were incidents where the same tactic was used not only in that one hospital but others and the PTT building and other buildings occupied by the UN." So it is a bit unclear. At least it didn't say "all hospitals," but that is the source, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. So I will ask my question in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This tactic that you refer to, did it also apply to other buildings but also, as I believe having heard, to all the hospitals as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness has not said, "all the hospitals." He has said --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but that is my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question whether this tactic -- if you look at the answer of the witness, it is not in all respects clear. Mr. Piletta-Zanin is now asking for a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I have no problem with that Mr. President. My concern is that now twice he has put to the witness that he has said "all". The key words in this question were "as I believe having heard."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "As I believe having heard."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, so the question is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I will retract that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would it apply to all hospitals.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Therefore, Witness, you meant two hospitals that we spoke about here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Kosevo because we were in situ. I heard from the operations room of the other hospital which we have discussed, the State Hospital, and that is as far as my statement goes, of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. And when you speak about the tactic, do you mean military strategy? Were you speaking about military strategy intended to provoke the fire of -- the adversary's fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD MOLE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could well be an element of the tactic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This then, Mr. Mole concludes your testimony in this court. I thank you very much, not only for coming, but even for coming back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is very unfortunate the way it went, but, well, we had no other choice. I am sorry for that. Thank you very much for coming. And I will ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. We will adjourn until a quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we still have to deal with a few procedural issues, I would rather do that now. Perhaps first the easy ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I suggest the very easy one of, first of all, tendering the exhibits in relation to Mr. Mole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That is also a procedural issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that regard, Mr. President, as I said yesterday, the only documents that I seek to tender are the three monthly reports. I think there is amongst them a confidential exhibit and the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the map is the pre-marked map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3689, under seal, end of month report October; Exhibit P358, end of month report November; Exhibit P618, end of month report December; Exhibit P3704, map premarked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, therefore, they are admitted into evidence. Then the second easy one. Mr. Stamp, I think it was you who -- or is there any other issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I merely wish to check. I had no time to check that, Mr. President. But is one of the exhibits indicated here, and these are the October and November, they were not -- they were not even shown to the witness. Or was it some other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All three were shown to the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, was there another document you said you would not tender, but these were not -- I would have to find them first. Yes. This is P354, which is not tendered, I take it. That is the daily sit-rep. And P511 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I don't propose to tender those two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think these were the two documents that would not be tendered. Yes. Then about the report of Dr. Zecevic, Professor Zecevic. I indicated already yesterday what the problem was. Mr. Stamp, I do understand that you deal with that. It is about the two annexes which are more or less reports of interviews, I think conducted by Mr. Tait-Harris, which is just text, no signatures, nothing else but text

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, they are in the nature of his responses to interrogatories in which he clarifies some of the matters that he raises in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On the other hand, I mean, if you have a typewriter, you could produce it. I mean, it is not in any way -- it is made after the report was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually, if we have written statements and that it is, as a matter of fact -- I do not have in my recollection that specifically there was any specific reference to those statements, apart from the report. I think he was asked whether the report was his.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand that that was the report that he made a couple of years ago. And then almost all the issues that appear in those statements, were dealt with during the examination. So I wonder what we should do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. The witness endorsed and adopted all five items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to check that then first, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if the issue is whether or not the Prosecution necessarily relies on those two latter reports of his responses which he has adopted, the simple practical and easy answer is no. There is a more complicated way of looking at it and that is a matter of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The issue being raised now is whether or not it is signed, and it is an issue which is raised in an untimely way, and if we concede that, then does it apply also to the curriculum vitae, which is not signed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may just briefly take us through the steps to how we got to this stage. The report was filed with five annexes -- I beg your pardon, the fourth statement, according to the Rules, was filed with five annexes, one being the report. An objection was formally made to it in the form of a motion made by the Defence. That was litigated. The Court made a decision on the 31st in which it clearly, I humbly submit, set out quite clearly and quite succinctly what the law was and what the position was: These annexes inclusive of the statement having been adopted by the witness was his full statement in accordance with the Rules. The witness came and he testified, and he adopted them. The Defence had an opportunity to cross-examine him. The issue was never raised in cross-examination. The question of their admission into evidence arose and the Defence raised the issue of certain references to air bombs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thereafter, it was determined that we would retract or redact that part. And at a late time when the witness has already departed these shores, the issue as to whether or not he has signed a couple of pages is raised.
